mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month indicates a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is above 2% annually, it indicates a supportive monetary policy in a growing economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and GDPC1 annual growth is above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a strong labor market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the past three months signals robust consumer demand, which is a strong indicator for economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at an annualized rate of more than 3%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy in an inflationary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 3% and CPIAUCSL annualized increase is more than 3%.
